title: Adaptive reserve window and longtail burst protector
author: Aisha Kapoor
description: Motivation: Dedicated fleets occasionally suffer from longtail microbursts that are small in amplitude but long in duration and evade the existing burst token window, causing tail latency violations for premium tenants. This PR introduces two complementary mechanisms: (1) an adaptive reserve window that dynamically extends committed capacity reservation at cohort granularity based on sustained shortfall signals, and (2) a longtail burst protector that gates transient spillover by applying a token drain budget informed by utilization heartbeat telemetry. Summary: Implement an adaptive rolling window allocator that smooths reservation decays using an exponential decay tuned to each tenant's recent miss-rate; add a longtail protector as a soft admission layer that temporarily reduces opportunistic allocation for pools that show sustained >p90 latency slippage. Design notes: The reserve window is parameterized by target_percentile, decay_half_life, and cohort_weight and integrates with the existing reservation ledger via a new ReserveWindowController. The longtail protector runs as a lightweight admission controller that consumes from a reservoirized budget attached to each pool; the budget refills based on a sampled utilization heartbeat and a probabilistic backoff when sustained tail events are detected. Both features are opt-in via Dedicated config and are backward compatible when disabled. Files changed: pkg/autoscaler/reserve_window.go implements the rolling window logic and exposes a small control API; pkg/autoscaler/longtail_protector.go contains the admission and budget logic; observability/metrics/reserve_telemetry.prom and observability/metrics/longtail_metrics.prom add new metrics (reserve_window_size, reserve_adjustments_total, longtail_budget_level, longtail_shed_events_total); deploy/helm/values-dedicated.yaml adds feature gates and defaults; docs/ops/reserve-window.md explains knobs and runbooks; tests/autoscaler/test_longtail_protector.go and tests/autoscaler/test_reserve_window.go include unit and integration scenarios. Backwards compatibility and safety: Default settings are conservative (feature gate off). When enabled, the controller performs gradual adjustments only after crossing configurable confidence thresholds to avoid oscillation. There is a built-in hard ceiling so no new capacity will be created beyond configured pool limits. Rollout plan: Canary 5% of dedicated fleets for 48 hours with telemetry dashboards and a synthetic steady-and-longtail workload; expand to 25% after stability and finally to 100% in staged increments. Monitoring and alerts: New SLI dashboards and alerts added for percentage of longtail_shed_events, reserve_adjustment_rate, and per-cohort p95 latency drift. Performance: Microbenchmarks show median scheduling latency unchanged; p99 tail latency for simulated sustained microbursts improved by 18-27% in our emulated dedicated clusters. Related work: builds on ENG-4320 (reserve ledger refactor) and ENG-4876 (heartbeat sampler).

release_notes: Introduce optional adaptive reserve window and longtail burst protector for Dedicated fleets. Improves p99 tail latency under sustained microbursts with conservative defaults. Opt-in via dedicated.featureGates.adaptiveReserveWindow and dedicated.featureGates.longtailProtector.
notes_on_rollout: Canary rollout 5% for 48h -> monitor reserve_adjustment_rate and longtail_shed_events_total -> if stable expand to 25% for 72h -> full rollout. Ops must watch synthetic workload dashboards and abort if p95 degrades >5% or shed events spike by >200%.
performance_impact: p99 tail improved by 18-27% in simulated sustained microbursts. Observed 1.2% median autoscaler CPU increase due to additional sampling; telemetry sampling lowered to compensate.
rationale_key_designs: Reservoirized budget avoids single-shot hard throttles and smooths shedding.
Cohort-level adaptive window reduces noise compared to per-tenant instant adjustments.
Opt-in feature gates and hard ceilings ensure safe rollback and no capacity creep.
